notes.title: Cube basics
notes.summary: How ESR uses the Horadric Cube, how to read the official recipe page, and the rules that make a recipe silently fail.

children.value: In ESR almost every upgrade is a cube recipe. The official Cube Recipes page is the full reference: sections of short rules followed by Input → Output tables. It is not a tutorial, so here is how to read it.
"Any …" means any item of that kind. "Torso" is body armor, "Armor" is every kind of armor.
"ilvl = char level" and similar lines give the output's item level, which decides the affixes it can roll.
Underlined materials in an output are handed back to you; removing a Forging, for example, returns its Anvil Stones.
Keys, Scrolls of Identify, Antidote Potions and the like often act as switches that pick which variant of a recipe runs.

notes.summary: Permanent stat boosts that raise an item's level requirement, and Secret Recipe 50 to lower it again so you can keep going.

children.value: cubes an item with one of the Dragon Stone forms, sometimes with a Key or potion as a switch, to add a small permanent stat (

the stat reaches its D-stoning cap, which counts only what D-stoning added (enhanced damage and defense can never pass 500% in total), or
the item's level requirement penalty reaches the fail-safe limit for its tier (normal and jewelry allow the most, elite the least).
D-stoning cannot be removed. It works on runewords too: done to the white base before you make the runeword, it survives removing the runes; done afterwards, it is lost with the runes.

Each cap counts only what D-stoning added: 190% fire spell damage from affixes still leaves room for the full +300%. A use applies while the D-stoned total is at or below the cap in the recipe, so the last use can go a few points past the official page's round number.

notes.title: Glossary
notes.summary: Short definitions of the ESR words used in this guide, each linked to the note that explains it.

children.value: New to the jargon? Each term links to the note that explains it;

entries.definition: A drop that names one vanilla (LoD) unique; matching coupons, alone or with Wild Cards, cube into that unique.
A common material that identifies Ancient Scrolls and feeds many recipes; eight make a Dragon Stone.
A numbered scroll (1 to 50) that unlocks the Secret Recipe with the same number; it is returned after each use.
A random bonus added with an Orb of Anointment (non-unique, non-runeword gear) or the three Demonic organs of the Prime Evils (unique charms); it cannot brick the item.
A stronger crafting stone made from Dragon Stones and a Perfect Gem; the main cost of Skill and Stat Forging.
A subclass specialisation granted by an Ascendancy Stone, upgraded through five tiers of challenges.
Decides whether attacks hit; ESR's curve gives 50% at 5 times the target's defense, with no 5% minimum or 95% maximum.

ESR's own damage over time, in place of vanilla's Open Wounds; physical hits make the target lose a percent of that hit's physical damage over a few seconds. The strongest bleed wins and it stacks with poison.
An ESR gem grade between Flawless and Perfect, used for rare rerolls, sockets on elite white bases and on exceptional items that are not white, and Ascendancy Stones.
A modifier on the copy that Inarius' Everburning Halo makes of an item (the original comes back unchanged); a Branded item can no longer be changed by any recipe.
The speed value (attack, cast, hit recovery or block) at which an animation gets one frame shorter; speed between breakpoints does nothing. The official Frame Table lists attack and cast breakpoints.
An item line that casts a skill at a set level on a trigger, such as on striking, on attack, when struck, on kill or, in ESR, on casting a skill.
A unique large charm that the official cube page lists in the Starter Pack; the 3.2.12 game files give no way to get one.
A cube recipe that turns a magic item, a class's Dragon Stone form, a Perfect Gem and a jewel into crafted gear with that class's skills.
Cubing an item with a Worldstone Shard for a random strong bonus, with a chance to turn the item into a random rare.
Cubing spare coupons with a Randomizing Stone to get a random coupon of the same or the next tier.

A chance on hit to remove a share of the target's current life, melee or ranged; in ESR 12.5% on normal monsters, 6.25% on yellow uniques, 2% on superuniques, 2% on act bosses, 5% on players and 5% on mercenaries.
One of twelve ESR socketable minerals (such as Frozen Soul or Pulsing Opal) in Chipped, Flawed and normal grades.
Cubing an item with a Dragon Stone form to add a small permanent stat at the cost of a higher level requirement.

A chance per hit to multiply the hit's physical damage, ×2 by default; Deadly Strike Damage raises the multiplier. Weapon-mastery crits, Critical Strike and Deadly Strike roll in turn and only one can succeed, so they never stack.
An ESR stat that adds to the ×2 crit multiplier of Deadly Strike, Critical Strike and weapon-mastery crits; +50% makes crits deal ×2.5.
A drop that, cubed with the ES rune named on it, becomes the vanilla (LoD) rune named on it.
ESR's grouped line for Dodge (melee, standing), Avoid (missiles, standing) and Evade (both, while moving); each is capped at 75%.
The main crafting stone of ESR, used for D-stoning, class crafts, many Secret Recipes and Anvil Stones.
The shapes a Dragon Stone cycles through when cubed alone (Holy Symbol, Blackmoor, Forging Hammer, Crushed Gem, Spider's Silk, Tyranium Ore, Void Shard); each is a different ingredient.
A consumable item that, transmuted alone in Act 5 Hell, opens a high-level zone, most of them with a boss; maps come in five tiers.
The "−% to Enemy X Resist" line on gear; lowers the target's resistance for your damage only, but does nothing against an immune monster.
ESR's own rune line, named after Japanese syllables from I up to Wo; used in ESR runewords, Rune Forging and many recipes.
A breakable urn that can stand in any area with monsters since 3.2.19 (2%, 4% and 6% of rooms in Normal, Nightmare and Hell); breaking it releases a boss pack whose boss has one extra rare affix.
ESR lets Faster Cast Rate count up to 500 instead of vanilla's 200; because of rounding nothing above 480 changes a breakpoint.
A cube recipe that adds one extra, removable bonus to an item; an item holds one Forging at a time.
Cubing an item with a Perfect Gem and Decipherers to add that gem's chipped bonus permanently, raising the level requirement.
A runeword-like recipe that uses gems instead of runes in a socketed white item or charm.
A monster at 100% or more resistance to a damage type takes no damage of that type; −% Enemy Resist cannot break it; curses, auras and Sunder effects can.
An ESR stat ("Increased Quantity of Items Found") that adds extra picks from a monster's own drops; 100% is one extra pick. Not on prime evils.
One of ESR's top socketables (Moon, Fire, Water up to God), made from a Null Rune and crystals.
A book from the Starter Pack that counts kills and takes permanent bonuses at kill milestones and after endgame boss kills.

Life or mana gained from a percent of the physical weapon damage you deal ("Physical Damage Leeched as Life/Mana"; elemental damage does not leech); for players it is divided by 25 and 150 (life) or 15 and 75 (mana) in Nightmare and Hell.
An ESR stat that gives flat life (or mana) on every hit that lands, melee or missile; unlike leech it has no difficulty penalty.
A vanilla rune (El to Zod), built from a Decal and an ES rune; used in the reworked vanilla runewords.

Raises the chance that drops are magic, rare, set or unique, never the number of drops; rare, set and unique get diminishing returns, plus an ESR bonus of 10% of your raw Magic Find. Items without a rarity (gems, runes, crystals, organs, keys, maps, Worldstone Shards) ignore it.
A material made mainly from spare unique charms; spent on Mapling, All Skill Forging and several high-end recipes.
Secret Recipe 50, which spends a Maple Leaf and a Perfect Gem to lower an item's level requirement penalty so it can be D-stoned again.
Raises one element's 75% resistance cap, up to a hard ceiling of 95%.
A cube recipe that gives a weapon or armor a bonus package only a mercenary can use; three Antidote Potions undo it.
The general stocker for organs, Dragon Stones, Decipherers, coupons, Maple Leaves and more; also turns spare set and unique gear into Decipherer points.
A top-tier unique that only drops in Endgame Maps, some of them from one specific boss.
The one-socket charm from the Starter Pack; Secret Recipe 49 turns it into a Veteran's Odd Charm.
A rune made from a Wo Rune and a Full Rejuvenation Potion; the base for every Kanji rune.
Monster parts (Hearts, Souls, Brains, Eyes, Scalps, Horns, Fangs, Jawbones, Spleens, Quills, Tails) used for tinkering, the Vessel of Souls and conversions.
A skill granted by an item that any class can use, such as the elemental Surges and Brands.
ESR's name for "Damage Reduced by %"; cuts physical damage you take, capped at 50%, and also weakens Crushing Blow against you.

A monster flagged primeevil in the game files (act bosses, ubers, endgame map bosses and a few others); players and their summons deal only 50% damage to them in Nightmare and 25% in Hell. Since 3.3 a launcher plugin makes terror zone heralds count as prime evils and bosses too.
A stocker for rings, amulets, jewels, charms and quivers that stores them as points by rarity and rerolls them into new ones.
The amount Nightmare and Hell subtract from your fire, cold, lightning and poison resistances; in ESR −80 and −150.
Using Lucion's Relic of Sanctification on a jewel (since 3.3 also a ring or amulet, with the Jeweler perk Hallowed Accessories) for a one-time bonus that cannot be undone.
One of the numbered cube recipes that only work with the matching identified Ancient Scroll in the cube.
Shortens skill cooldowns; each skill stops at a floor, on most skills 20% of the base cooldown.
The cube ingredient that adds sockets to an item, together with gems whose grade matches the item tier.
A container item that destroys the materials you cube into it and stores them as points you can take out later.

An area currently terrorized, with stronger monsters; terrorized champions and uniques can drop Worldstone Shards, and terrorized superuniques and act bosses at monster level 96 can drop Endgame Maps. Since 3.3 every zone belongs to a terror group, and each group includes one Endgame Map.
A potion used, three at a time, to remove a Forging from an item; it also appears in key and charm recipes.
Cubing gear with organs to add small permanent bonuses, limited by the tinkering points shown on each item.
A consumable made from Dragon Stones; right-click it to add one respec to the character's respec counter.
A mythical amulet that you feed organs in the cube to build up bonuses, then turn into a mythical weapon; it is not meant to be worn.
A removable specialisation applied to a class weapon with an awakened Weapon Mastery Token; it changes how skills work with that weapon.
A joker made from spare coupons that stands in for the third matching coupon in unique recipes (higher tiers need more of them) and appears in several gem recipes.

A stronger crafting stone made from Dragon Stones and a Perfect Gem; the main cost of Skill and Stat Forging.
A cube recipe that adds one extra, removable bonus to an item; an item holds one Forging at a time.
A potion used, three at a time, to remove a Forging from an item; it also appears in key and charm recipes.
Cubing an item with a Dragon Stone form to add a small permanent stat at the cost of a higher level requirement.

A material made mainly from spare unique charms; spent on Mapling, All Skill Forging and several high-end recipes.

A cube recipe that gives a weapon or armor a bonus package only a mercenary can use; three Antidote Potions undo it.
A skill granted by an item that any class can use, such as the elemental Surges and Brands.
A cube recipe that turns a magic item, a class's Dragon Stone form, a Perfect Gem and a jewel into crafted gear with that class's skills.
A breakable urn that can stand in any area with monsters since 3.2.19 (2%, 4% and 6% of rooms in Normal, Nightmare and Hell); breaking it releases a boss pack whose boss has one extra rare affix.

A chance per hit to multiply the hit's physical damage, ×2 by default; Deadly Strike Damage raises the multiplier. Weapon-mastery crits, Critical Strike and Deadly Strike roll in turn and only one can succeed, so they never stack.
An ESR stat that adds to the ×2 crit multiplier of Deadly Strike, Critical Strike and weapon-mastery crits; +50% makes crits deal ×2.5.

A chance on hit to remove a share of the target's current life, melee or ranged; in ESR 12.5% on normal monsters, 6.25% on yellow uniques, 2% on superuniques, 2% on act bosses, 5% on players and 5% on mercenaries.

ESR's own damage over time, in place of vanilla's Open Wounds; physical hits make the target lose a percent of that hit's physical damage over a few seconds. The strongest bleed wins and it stacks with poison.

Life or mana gained from a percent of the physical weapon damage you deal ("Physical Damage Leeched as Life/Mana"; elemental damage does not leech); for players it is divided by 25 and 150 (life) or 15 and 75 (mana) in Nightmare and Hell.
An ESR stat that gives flat life (or mana) on every hit that lands, melee or missile; unlike leech it has no difficulty penalty.
ESR's name for "Damage Reduced by %"; cuts physical damage you take, capped at 50%, and also weakens Crushing Blow against you.
The amount Nightmare and Hell subtract from your fire, cold, lightning and poison resistances; in ESR −80 and −150.
Raises one element's 75% resistance cap, up to a hard ceiling of 95%.
A monster at 100% or more resistance to a damage type takes no damage of that type; −% Enemy Resist cannot break it; curses, auras and Sunder effects can.
The "−% to Enemy X Resist" line on gear; lowers the target's resistance for your damage only, but does nothing against an immune monster.
Decides whether attacks hit; ESR's curve gives 50% at 5 times the target's defense, with no 5% minimum or 95% maximum.
An item line that casts a skill at a set level on a trigger, such as on striking, on attack, when struck, on kill or, in ESR, on casting a skill.
The speed value (attack, cast, hit recovery or block) at which an animation gets one frame shorter; speed between breakpoints does nothing. The official Frame Table lists attack and cast breakpoints.
ESR lets Faster Cast Rate count up to 500 instead of vanilla's 200; because of rounding nothing above 480 changes a breakpoint.
ESR's grouped line for Dodge (melee, standing), Avoid (missiles, standing) and Evade (both, while moving); each is capped at 75%.

Raises the chance that drops are magic, rare, set or unique, never the number of drops; rare, set and unique get diminishing returns, plus an ESR bonus of 10% of your raw Magic Find. Items without a rarity (gems, runes, crystals, organs, keys, maps, Worldstone Shards) ignore it.
An ESR stat ("Increased Quantity of Items Found") that adds extra picks from a monster's own drops; 100% is one extra pick. Not on prime evils.
Shortens skill cooldowns; each skill stops at a floor, on most skills 20% of the base cooldown.

A monster flagged primeevil in the game files (act bosses, ubers, endgame map bosses and a few others); players and their summons deal only 50% damage to them in Nightmare and 25% in Hell. Since 3.3 a launcher plugin makes terror zone heralds count as prime evils and bosses too.
